stem.text: The speed shown on a car’s speedometer is proportional to the rate of rotation of the tyres.
The variation of the diameter of a tyre as it wears introduces an error in the speed shown on the speedometer.
A car has new tyres of diameter $600\,\text{mm}$. The speedometer is accurately calibrated for this diameter.
The tyres wear as shown, with $6\,\text{mm}$ of material being removed from the outer surface.

stem.alt: Diagram of a tyre cross-section outline, not to scale: a solid arc labelled worn tyre and a dashed arc labelled new tyre, with a 6 mm arrow between them.

stem.text: What is the error in the speed shown on the speedometer after this wear has taken place?

A.text: The speed shown is too high by 1%.

B.text: The speed shown is too high by 2%.

C.text: The speed shown is too low by 1%.

D.text: The speed shown is too low by 2%.
